name: V-Squat Machine
description: The V-squat machine guides the lifter along a fixed V-shaped arc, placing the load on shoulder pads while the feet remain on the floor or a low platform in front of the body. The angled path of the machine produces a movement pattern that is deeper than a standard hack squat machine while keeping the spine supported. It is a popular alternative to the squat and leg press for lifters who want significant quad loading with reduced spinal loading.

execution.starting_position: Step into the machine, positioning the shoulder pads on your shoulders. Feet on the platform, hip-width apart. Stand upright with the machine unlatched.
execution.setup_instructions: Adjust shoulder pads to fit comfortably. Set foot position on the platform to target quad emphasis (higher = more glute) or quad (lower feet).
steps: Step 1: Unlatch the machine and control the descent by bending the knees along the guided arc.
Step 2: Descend until the thighs reach at least parallel to the floor or deeper if flexibility allows.
Step 3: Drive through the heels and quads to press upward along the arc to the starting position.
Step 4: Lock out at the top without hyperextending the knees.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on descent, exhale on ascent.
safety_considerations: Engage the safety latches before stepping in or out of the machine
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Thighs to at least parallel; full depth preferred if mobility allows.
coaching_cues: Full depth — don't stop at parallel
